newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond issues may heat up ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond issues may heat up ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Corporate bond market players expect primary activity to pick up considerably in the days before a possible hike in official interest rates is debated at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"People are much more constructive, they want to come to market," said one syndicate desk dealer. "It's a timing thing," the dealer said, noting "corporates had a big week last week.

Issuance on Tuesday was topped by SunTrust Banks Inc's $250 million 10-year subordinated note deal. The notes, rated A1/A-plus, were given a 7.25 percent coupon and priced at par to yield 48.5 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury.
Looking ahead, "The calendar is building, the environment is good," the dealer said, adding "Most (new issues) are placed quickly."

Traders said Tuesday morning's slide in U.S. Treasuries should not have much affect on the corporate market. The yield on the 30-year bond hit seven percent when a Reuters story quoted a source at the Federal Reserve as saying the consensus within the Fed was for a 25 basis point rate hike on September 24.
One source at a syndicate desk said downward pressure in Treasuries "could temper the calendar, but there's still a bid to the market" for corporate primary issues.
Key Bank of Oregon also came to market on Tuesday, pricing $70 million 7-3/8 percent subordinated bank notes 99.50 to yield 7.438 percent.
The spread is 70 basis points over the 10-year Treasury.
Ford Motor Credit is expected to price a $1 billion global Eurobond deal as early as Tuesday. Dealers said the price talk is 48 to 50 basis points over the five-year Treasury.

Dealers also expect NationsBank Corp to announce a three-part deal totaling $1.4 billion. The deal would be comprised of $500 million of five year bonds, $550 million of ten year bonds and $350 million of 20 year bonds.

Daimler-Benz AG is one closely watched upcoming issuance, according to market players. Talk on trading floors is for $500 million in 10-year notes, rated at A1A-plus, with a 50-55 basis point spread. JP Morgan Securities will be the lead dealer.
Anadarko Petroleum Corp is expected to announce a 100-year issue with a 30-year put.
